operations.title: Graph Reasoning vs Memory Products: Field Gap and Personal KG Opportunity
operations.content: KG fine-tuning field consensus discovered (id:23364a94): everyone flattens the graph into text and tries to enrich it enough for LLM learning. Every approach loses structure in translation. But the research exists at top venues: Paths-over-Graph (id:516ec716) explores multi-hop reasoning, Graph-Constrained Reasoning enables decoding constraints, ReMindRAG adds memory replay loops, FastKGE incremental LoRA allocation. The gap nobody occupies (id:e51cc55a): memory projects (Mem0, GBrain) solve storage + retrieval with zero training; graph reasoning papers solve multi-hop reasoning over massive KGs with custom training. Personal knowledge graphs sit between them — too structured for memory products, too personal for academic benchmarks (id:dbc297b0). The barrier isn't technical (techniques transfer), it's community non-overlap: memory people don't read ICML papers, graph people don't build consumer products. This is the brain's unique position — 2000 nodes, 10K edges, 114 communities, rich enough for graph traversal reasoning but small enough to train on laptop. Apply PoG's path exploration, GCR's constrained decoding, FastKGE's incremental LoRA to personal knowledge. The techniques exist. The personal brain application doesn't — yet.

operations.title: Data Storage Unification: From Silent Failures to Atomic Metadata Paths
operations.content: The remember() extra_fields silent drop bug (id:d95fb32a) traces to fragmented storage logic — remember() and revise() each had separate metadata paths, causing remember() to accept parameters it never stored. Community metadata (narrative, maturity, hub_node_ids) disappeared silently since April 13. Fix unified storage through _store_node_metadata() (id:d399c342), single function handling both remember() and revise() paths. Expanded to archive_node() (id:614ebb66) which now handles full cleanup atomically: edges, vectors, FTS index, audit trail. Before: cleanup scattered across four modules (brain_remember.py, daemon_dispatch.py, consolidation_decoder.py, brain_assembly.py). Now: one call guarantees consistency. Used to clean 1022 archived nodes and 136 lean communities in same session. Pattern: silent failures happen when code paths diverge. Unification prevents drift. The lesson: metadata must have one source of truth, archival must be atomic, scattered logic creates hidden bugs waiting for edge cases.

operations.title: Dead Code Unification: From Dual Traversal Functions to Single Interface
operations.content: The get_neighbors unification (id:a2e33fe7) consolidated two functions into a single get_neighbors() interface, collapsing 180+ lines of dead code (_traverse_graph() + format_node_deep()) (id:eb99497c). The pattern revealed: dual-path graph traversal with zero external callers (id:4899a5e4) represents migration artifact — code paths that survive refactoring but serve no purpose. This differs from the write-only systems pattern (nodes created but never read) — here, code exists but zero call sites activate it. The consolidation reinforces the principle from Development Operations: dead code removal is a structural enforcement mechanism, not cleanup. Once removed, the system forces all traversal through a single validated path. Lesson: code paths without callers are invisible technical debt that prevents future architectural clarity.
operations.situation: When refactoring graph traversal or consolidating duplicate interfaces — audit for zero-caller functions, merge paths into single validated entry point, verify all call sites migrate
